# JOURNAL — optimizer handover (append-only, whole run)

YOU (the optimizer) own this file. It is the running, accumulating handover across ALL iterations — accepted AND rejected — and it is NEVER reset. Each iteration you APPEND one new entry at the bottom (under the marker line); you do NOT edit or delete earlier entries. Read the whole journal before proposing, so you build on EVERY prior attempt (not just the last accepted one) and never re-test a refuted idea.

You CANNOT know your own gate result while you write — the harness scores you AFTER you stop and stamps a **RESULT** line (outcome + Δ + the EXACT tasks you broke/fixed) right below your entry. So do NOT write 'what worked' as a guess. To learn what actually worked, READ the framework RESULT lines of prior entries (and LEDGER.md): an entry whose RESULT says `rejected` with `broke={...}` tells you which specific edits to drop or redesign — its diff.patch is in ./prior_iterations/<id>/.

Append your entry for THIS iteration below the marker, using this shape (INTENT only — the framework appends the RESULT):

    ## Iteration <your candidate id> — <one-line headline of what you tried>
    - Changes I made (1 line per edit; name the file/tool + cluster it targets):
    - Per change, the EXPECTED effect + why it's safe (which failing task it should fix;
      why no passing task changes behavior):
    - Building on prior RESULTS: which prior entries' broke/fixed I used, and what I
      did NOT re-try because a prior RESULT showed it regressed (cite ids):
    - Refuted hypotheses (a prior RESULT proved this is NOT the fix — never re-test):
    - High-value clusters still NOT cracked (and the guard/tool designs already tried):
    - Plateau signal (are the last few RESULTs flat/negative? if so, which LEVER to switch
      to — e.g. a NEW composite tool instead of another guard, or prompt instead of code):
    - Focus next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001 (seed child) — diagnosed val as a host-mount infra bug; one bounded anti-stall prompt rule
- Changes I made:
  - prompt.md: added a rule distinguishing a CODE error (fix & retry) from an ENVIRONMENT error on
    the fixed input/output paths (PermissionError / read-only mount / bind-mount write-denied) — in
    that case do NOT probe the sandbox for rounds; emit one complete solution to output_path and stop.
    Plus a positive anti-stall line: emit ONE self-contained final code block, don't narrate a plan
    across rounds without executing. Targets the only prompt-addressable behavior in the traces.
- Per change, expected effect + why it's safe:
  - I do NOT expect this to raise the score, because the true blocker is environmental (see below).
    It is safe/BOUNDED: in a healthy env no PermissionError fires → the env-error branch never
    triggers → zero behavior change on any task that would pass. It only shortens wasted looping on
    the broken env. Purely additive; loosens no decision rule.
- ROOT-CAUSE DIAGNOSIS (the important part): ALL 50 val tasks fail identically, reward 0.000, from a
  host-side bind-mount permission bug. `/mnt/data` is `drwx------ uid=1004` while the code kernel runs
  as `uid=1000`; the container can neither read inputs nor write outputs. 42/50 carry the runner error
  `"sandbox denied writes to the bind-mounted output dir ... not writable by the container's uid; see
  _make_container_writable"`; the other 8 hit the same wall. The "8 controllable vs 42 infra" split is
  spurious — same cause. Agents already tried chmod/chown/sudo/os.access/setuid/namei/find/`/tmp` — all
  denied. This CANNOT be fixed from the system prompt (the only editable artifact). It needs a RUNNER
  fix: make `/mnt/data` and the per-task output subdirs owned by / writable by the container uid
  (`_make_container_writable`).
- Building on prior RESULTS: none — this is the seed; LEDGER/RUNMAP/JOURNAL have no prior results.
- Refuted hypotheses: n/a (first iteration). But NOTE for the next optimizer: do NOT waste an
  iteration adding spreadsheet-correctness prompt rules — there is NO correctness signal in these
  traces; every failure is the permission wall. The seed's solution CODE was already correct on
  inspected tasks (e.g. 30709 produced a correct date-extraction solution on round 1).
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: the entire val set — blocked by the infra bug above. Nothing
  in the prompt can move it.
- Plateau signal: if the re-score of this candidate is still 0.000 across all 50 (expected while the
  mount stays 0700/uid-mismatched), the correct action is NOT another prompt lever — it is to FIX THE
  RUNNER MOUNT PERMISSIONS, then re-run. Only after the env is healthy will prompt/capability edits
  have any signal to optimize against.
- Focus next iteration: verify the mount fix landed (inputs readable + outputs writable by the kernel
  uid); only then diagnose real spreadsheet-correctness clusters.

> **RESULT (framework, objective):** REJECTED (champion unchanged) · val=0.000 Δ=+0.000 · fixed={—} · broke={—}. — its WHOLE batch was reverted; re-introduce only the edits that did NOT break a task above, dropping/redesigning the ones that did.
